subject: Finexus: production throttle + elevated errors — immediate remediation plan
messages:
From: Carlos Ramos <carlos.ramos@finexus.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: support@finexus.com
Date: 2027-06-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [URGENT] Finexus production: high latency, errors, and throughput drop

Jonas —

We just started seeing a sustained 18–22% increase in end-to-end latency and a 12% error rate spike on our payment confirmation path around 08:45 PT. Metrics show our reserved throughput is being metered below our committed rate (we're seeing ~60% of expected tokens/sec) and many requests are getting 503s. This is impacting settlement windows for merchants and we've already had two timeouts in the last 30 minutes.

Attached are a short span of server logs and our dashboard exports. Can you confirm whether this is a customer-side regression or a platform saturation issue? We need a mitigation plan and ETA — Finexus is preparing to pause a high-valued batch job if this isn't resolved within 2 hours.

Please escalate as needed.

-Carlos

Subject: Fwd: [URGENT] Finexus production: high latency, errors, and throughput drop

Folks — forwarding Carlos' note. This is hitting their reserved GPU pool (high priority customer, committed reserved capacity). Key asks: 1) immediate mitigation to restore committed throughput, 2) cause analysis, 3) timeline + customer comms.

Initial observations from our monitoring:
- Token throughput for their reserved pool dropped ~40% vs baseline at 08:44 PT.
- Error rate spike concentrated on the scorer/resize path (503s from inference nodes).
- Concurrent background jobs from another tenant were visible in the same pool window (suspect noisy neighbor on dedicated shards).

Proposed immediate action (please confirm and execute):
- Aditya: enable short-term routing to a hot spare hosted pool and enforce strict rate caps to protect their SLA while we investigate (we can route only their high-priority routes).
- Marissa/Naomi: prep customer-facing note and propose 7 days of credit if we miss the SLA window; schedule exec call if Carlos wants one.
- We should also consider transiently lifting placement constraints for this customer's reserved pool to move sensitive shards out of crowded hardware.

I will schedule a 30-min bridge at 11:30 PT unless you flag urgency sooner.

-JW
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-29T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: [URGENT] Finexus production: high latency, errors, and throughput drop

Jonas / team —

Thanks for flagging. Ops dug in and here's what we see and propose (short and medium term):

What we see:
- Two large background inference scans from partner-tenant "X-Scout" started at 08:30 and overlapped with Finexus' peak. They consumed long sequence runs and exhausted KV cache lanes on a subset of nodes, causing queueing for reserved workloads.
- Autoscaler did not add capacity because the workload pattern looked like long-running, low-concurrency jobs (we're tuning threshold logic).

Immediate (<= 90m):
- Activate emergency burst routing: move Finexus high-priority routes to a pre-warmed hosted hot pool for ~2 hours. This will restore latency and reserved throughput while preserving data isolation for the critical route.
- Kill or throttle the overlapping X-Scout jobs on the shared placement; Ops will coordinate with partner team to reschedule.
- Warm KV cache on the branched nodes and restart the affected inference workers to clear queueing.

Mitigation tradeoffs:
- Burst routing incurs short-term extra cost on our side; recommend we offer 7 days of pro-rated credit and a technical post-mortem.
- There's a minor risk (~5%) that moving shards will bump cold-start latency for a handful of requests — acceptable given current impacts.

Naomi, please prepare a customer note. Aditya, can you confirm the steps and estimated time for the worker restarts and hot-pool cutover?

-M
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-29T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Re: Fwd: [URGENT] Finexus production: high latency, errors, and throughput drop

Quick tech note / runbook:

Confirmed root cause (preliminary): KV cache exhaustion + long-sequence jobs from X-Scout reducing effective concurrency on shared NUMA nodes. The inference workers began queueing new streams, producing 503s under backpressure.

What I'm executing now (live):
1) Flip routing rule to send Finexus.high-priority -> hosted-hot-pool (rollback toggle ready).
2) Scale up hosted-hot-pool by +3 instances (pre-warmed images).
3) Restart affected inference workers on 4 nodes (drain, restart, rejoin) — will clear internal queueing and allow cache warming.
4) Set temporary soft-rate cap of 120% of their committed token/sec to prevent burst storms during cutover.

ETA: 60–90 minutes for full restoration to observed baseline; partial improvement expected in ~15–20 minutes after cutover begins.

Risks: restarting workers could surface rare model cold-start errors; I will watch logs. If we see regression we will rollback routing and open a narrower remediation (per-node warm-up).

I'll post updates to the drive link and call out any need for exec escalation.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Carlos Ramos <carlos.ramos@finexus.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-29T10:32:00-07:00
Subject: RE: [URGENT] Finexus production: high latency, errors, and throughput drop

Carlos —

Thank you for the signal and the logs. We're treating this as a priority incident. Summary of actions already in flight:
- Ops has identified noisy long-sequence jobs from another tenant that caused KV cache pressure and queueing on shared nodes.
- We're performing an emergency cutover of Finexus high-priority routes to a pre-warmed hosted hot pool (live now).
- We are restarting affected inference workers and warming caches; Aditya estimates 60–90 minutes to fully restore committed throughput, with partial gains visible within 15–20 minutes.

Customer-facing commitments:
- We'll follow up with a technical post-mortem within 48 hours.
- If we fail to meet the committed throughput SLA within the window we will issue 7 days of pro-rated service credit; Naomi will send the formal credit note.

We understand the impact on your settlement windows — I have a 11:30 PT bridge on the calendar (invitation is being sent) to walk through next steps and answer questions. If you need an earlier exec-level call please let me know and we'll escalate.

Apologies again — we are on it.

Best,
